summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ , a man with secondary progressive multiple sclerosis and a history of recurrent urinary tract infections, was admitted with weakness, decreased oral intake, and lightheadedness, symptoms typical of his usual UTI presentations. He performs self-catheterization but with suboptimal hygiene practices. Initial evaluation showed no fever or leukocytosis, and a chest X-ray revealed no acute process. Urine culture grew Klebsiella pneumoniae sensitive to multiple antibiotics, including ciprofloxacin and meropenem. He was treated with IV meropenem during hospitalization, with improvement in symptoms. Blood cultures showed no growth. He received education on proper catheterization technique to reduce future infection risk. He was discharged home with services on a 14-day course of oral ciprofloxacin and instructions to restart methenamine hippurate after completing antibiotics, with follow-up arranged.
